purpose: Earlier work this version extends, and a comparison of the ledger with the catalogue of the IEA 4E review (P01). Values attributed to P01 are transcribed as P01 records them, with ranges written 'x to y' and thousands separated by commas; they are not re-verified against the publications P01 reviewed.

four_e_parameters.four_e_values: academia, government, industry, non-governmental organisation, mixed
four_e_parameters.ledger: No field. The publisher is named in forecaster; its affiliation type is not recorded.
No field. The catalogue's source_type records whether a source is a primary document or table, not its publication type.
geography names the area covered: Global and US in the ledger; the candidates add the Australian National Electricity Market, Europe and China as the IEA defines them, France and Denmark.

horizon records the target year; a historical estimate carries the metric historical_model_estimate and stays outside spans; forecast_vintage, source_publication and base_year record dates separately.

four_e_parameters.four_e_values: bottom-up, aggregated totals, temporal proxy extrapolation, hybrid, other
four_e_parameters.ledger: method_description records the method only in wording located in the source and assigns no class; model_reproduction records that no provider model was rebuilt.

four_e_parameters.four_e_values: data centre types (enterprise, cloud, hyperscale) and specific technologies or topics (AI)
four_e_parameters.ledger: coverage records the facility boundary and crypto_scope the cryptocurrency boundary; data-centre types appear in qualifications where the source states them.

four_e_parameters.parameter: Recorded by P01 outside the six parameters
four_e_parameters.four_e_values: starting, ending and base year of each assessment; one row per named scenario; cryptocurrency removed where an assessment included it; emissions-only results converted to electricity
four_e_parameters.ledger: base_year and scenario are recorded as stated; crypto_scope records the stated or inferred boundary and nothing is removed; no conversion between quantities is made.

four_e_parameters.parameter: Ledger fields with no P01 catalogue parameter
four_e_parameters.four_e_values: P01's metric is annual energy consumption in TWh
four_e_parameters.ledger: unit and metric distinguish energy, capacity, capacity demand and growth; value_basis records table, text or chart values; shape records points, ranges and bounds; superseded_by and comparison_family record same-publisher vintages; SUPPORT_REVIEW.json binds an independent receipt to each row.

four_e_comparison.four_e_entries: IEA (2014) to IEA (2025); the latest are Electricity 2024, World Energy Outlook 2024 and Electricity 2025
four_e_comparison.four_e_record: Global, IEA (2024b) with Spencer and Singh (2024): 240 to 340 TWh in 2022 and a 2030 projection of 515 TWh (range 405 to 685 TWh)
four_e_comparison.four_e_scenario: range given; scenario names not given in the table
four_e_comparison.four_e_crypto: excluding cryptocurrency, as P01 records it
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; Table 3.1, p. 16; references, p. 55
four_e_comparison.difference: Different editions. P01's latest global IEA projection comes from the World Energy Outlook 2024; the ledger registers the tabulated Base Case values of the 2025 Energy and AI annex and the 2026 report, which P01 does not list. P01 records its IEA values as excluding cryptocurrency; the ledger records cryptocurrency coverage for its IEA rows as not stated. Not a revision comparison.

four_e_comparison.four_e_entries: Shehabi et al. (2016, 2018, 2024); the latest is the 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
four_e_comparison.four_e_record: United States, Shehabi et al. (2024): 178 TWh in 2023 and 325 to 580 TWh in 2028
four_e_comparison.four_e_scenario: range given; scenario names not given in the table
four_e_comparison.four_e_crypto: excluding cryptocurrency, as P01 states for this report
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; section 3.2.1, p. 20; Table 3.2, p. 23; references, p. 60
four_e_comparison.difference: Earlier edition of the same report series: P01 covers the 2024 report and the ledger registers the 2025 Update. Both record cryptocurrency as excluded. The values come from different editions and are not compared as a revision.

four_e_comparison.four_e_record: United States: a 2030 projection of 200 to 405 TWh
four_e_comparison.four_e_scenario: range from assumed growth rates; scenario names not given in the table
four_e_comparison.four_e_crypto: not stated for this entry; P01's US figure note says its US values exclude cryptocurrencies
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; Figure 3.3 note, p. 21; Table 3.2, p. 22; references, p. 52
four_e_comparison.difference: Earlier edition of the same series: P01 covers the 2024 report and the ledger registers the 2026 brief. The ledger records the 2026 range as including cryptocurrency, while P01's US figure note says its US values exclude cryptocurrencies. Not compared as a revision.

four_e_comparison.four_e_entries: McKinsey (2023), (2024a) and (2024b); McKinsey (2024a) carries the URL of ledger source S05
four_e_comparison.four_e_record: United States, McKinsey (2024a): 147 TWh in 2023, 178 TWh in 2024 (25 GW capacity) and a 2030 projection of 606 TWh (80 GW)
four_e_comparison.four_e_crypto: not stated for this entry; P01's US figure note says its US values exclude cryptocurrencies
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; section 3.2.1, p. 20; Table 3.2, p. 23; references, p. 58
four_e_comparison.difference: Same publication and the same 2030 value. P01 also records a 2030 capacity figure and 2023 and 2024 values, which the ledger does not register. The ledger records the medium scenario and a cryptocurrency exclusion inferred from the publication's footnote; P01's table states neither. McKinsey's four other registered figures come from later publications.

four_e_comparison.four_e_base_year: not given as such; P01's method summary says the global projection builds on the high range of an IEA estimate for 2022
four_e_comparison.four_e_entries: Goldman Sachs (2024), AI, data centers and the coming US power demand surge
four_e_comparison.four_e_record: Global: a 2030 projection of 740 to 1,400 TWh; United States: 397 TWh in 2030
four_e_comparison.four_e_scenario: Base Case, Bear and Bull (Figure 3.1 legend)
four_e_comparison.four_e_quality: global: medium; United States: not assessed
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; Figure 3.1, p. 13; Table 3.1, p. 15; Table 3.2, p. 22; references, p. 53
four_e_comparison.difference: Different publications and quantities. P01 records annual energy in TWh from Goldman Sachs's 2024 report; the ledger registers later statements of power-demand growth relative to a base year, which it does not convert to energy.

four_e_comparison.four_e_entries: BloombergNEF, Statkraft and Eaton (2021), Data Centers and Decarbonization
four_e_comparison.four_e_record: Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway and the United Kingdom: 26 TWh in 2021 for colocation and hyperscale data centres
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; Table 3.3, p. 25; references, p. 49
four_e_comparison.difference: No overlap of edition, geography or quantity: P01 covers a 2021 European energy estimate, and the ledger registers BloombergNEF's 2025 and 2026 US installed-capacity forecasts.

four_e_comparison.four_e_entries: S&P Global (2024), S&P Global Commodity Insights (2024) and S&P Global Market Intelligence (2024a), the 2024 US Datacenters and Energy Report
four_e_comparison.four_e_record: United States: Commodity Insights, 355 to 385 TWh in 2030; Market Intelligence, over 280 TWh in 2024 and 530 TWh in 2028; S&P Global, 340 to 420 TWh in 2030
four_e_comparison.four_e_crypto: not stated for these entries; P01's US figure note says its US values exclude cryptocurrencies
four_e_comparison.four_e_quality: Commodity Insights: medium; the other two: not assessed
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; Table 3.2, p. 24; references, p. 61
four_e_comparison.difference: Earlier publications only. P01 covers S&P Global's 2024 reports; the ledger registers the 2026 outlook and a June 2026 webinar report. The 2024 report and the 2026 outlook have similar titles, but the retained records do not establish that they form one series, so they are not treated as editions of one series.

four_e_comparison.four_e_record: Global: 380 TWh in 2023 and a 2030 range of 700 to 970 TWh
four_e_comparison.four_e_quality: medium-high; P01 names it as the exception among consultancy and investment-bank studies
four_e_comparison.four_e_locator: P01 Table 2.1, p. 5; Figure 3.1, p. 13; Table 3.1, p. 14; section 5.2.2, p. 39; references, p. 51
four_e_comparison.difference: Different Deloitte publications of late 2024. P01 records the 2030 range of Deloitte Global's Powering AI; the ledger registers the 2030 figure in Deloitte's 2025 predictions article, which lies outside that range. The retained records do not establish whether the two share a model.
